profile.purpose: Design the binder arm with BindCraft2 running as a local process on an installation the scientist owns, and screen its output on the inherited ESMFold2-Fast predictor, rebound here to its own local route. No stage of this profile reaches a network service, so it asks for no provider endpoint at all. This is one reproducible configuration rather than a general BindCraft2 substitute: it fixes --core benchmark and --modality binder, exposes neither --property nor --set, and the adapter refuses a multi-chain binder modality because the lane has no rule for publishing one.

The same adapter module has run: the 2026-09-02 Modal v14 shard invoked claude_binder.adapters.esmfold2_fast_predictor directly and its receipt reports ok true with no errors, settling at 0.02712564 USD per fold on a Modal L40S. stage_overrides.description: Design the BindCraft2 arm end to end on an installation the scientist owns: AlphaFold 2 sequence optimization on the ColabDesign framework, the tool's own ProteinMPNN redesign, and validation with separate AlphaFold models and structural filters. The stage validates every modality, property, core profile and setting name against the installed copy's own --list-* output before it starts the subprocess, and it runs --core benchmark so the seed is pinned and the adaptive tuning is off. No sequence-design stage follows, because the generator designs the sequence. Acceptance is the tool's own computational verdict, so every published row stays status generated and the lane's own screen ranks it. The argv names --modality binder deliberately. Upstream applies no modality layer when none is named, and naming binder reads settings/modality/binder.json, which bans cysteine through aa_bias, sets min_monomer_plddt_final to 0.7 and adds a Binder_RMSD filter at 3.5. The composed binder_lengths override the preset's own range, because the request is the last layer upstream applies.
